Hi Sara / Tom,

Thanks again for the time today — appreciate the clear overview of HealthSecure's priorities. Per our call, I put together a short recap of the discussion, pain points, and next steps. Please flag anything I missed.

Summary of pain points / drivers
- Regulatory requirement: PHI must remain inside customer-controlled VPCs for production workloads; no tokenized PHI may be written to third-party storage.
- Network constraints: staging must be air-gapped for SOC/PCI workflows; limited outbound egress from production subnets; strict allowlist policy.
- Key management: customer-controlled KMS/HSM requirement and auditability for encryption keys and signing.
- Ops: need for audit logs (request-level) retained 12 months and fine-grained RBAC for model operations.

Goals / success criteria
1) Private deployment (VPC or on-prem) with a customer-managed control plane or an allowed private control plane instance.
2) No external egress from production model hosts; ability to route telemetry/logging to customer-owned systems (Splunk/Datadog).
3) Achieve SOC2 + HIPAA controls for production by the time of pilot (target: Feb 2027).
4) Demonstrate a vetted air-gap installation for staging/dev within 6-8 weeks for an initial POC.

Technical notes from the call
- We confirmed that Redwood's Private offering supports a VPC-deployed control plane and an air-gapped on-prem package (we discussed the installer + manifest approach).
- For low-latency inference we recommend colocating model hosts in the same VPC subnets you use for inference clients.
- Marissa will follow up with a short checklist of required ports and a sample network diagram (see attachment).

Attachments (sent with this email)
- HealthSecure_Security_Reqs.xlsx — your answers to the questionnaire you shared in the call. (Tom: thanks for sending.)
- redwood_private_vpc_overview.pdf — high-level flow for private deployments and KMS integration.

Immediate next steps
- Action: Mateo to produce an initial network diagram and required allowlist (ETA: 10/13).
- Action: Camila to share procurement contacts and an overview of pricing for a reserved Dedicated + Private deployment (ETA: 10/14).
- Action: HealthSecure to confirm which environment needs air-gap first (staging or pre-prod) and provide the infra contact for scheduling a technical deep-dive.

Proposed follow-up
- 60-min tech deep-dive with your infra/security leads and our solutions engineering team (Marissa, Mateo) — suggested slots next week (10/14 or 10/15).

Thanks — I’ll wait on the infra contact and will circulate the calendar options once I hear back.

Best,
Camila Reyes

Sara / team — quick technical notes from our side (adding Mateo on the thread):

1) Air-gap / staging installer
- We provide an air-gapped installer bundle (tarball + install guide) that can be staged on an internal repo. Installation requires an internal registry for images (we support both containerd and dockerd).
- For configuration we support customer KMS integrations (AWS KMS, HashiCorp Vault HSM, Azure Key Vault).

2) Network / allowlist (high level)
- Required outbound (if allowed): to your internal telemetry endpoints only (no external SaaS endpoints).
- Ports between control plane and model hosts: 443 (TLS) for control-plane hooks, and higher-throughput gRPC ports (50051/tcp) for model traffic inside the VPC. We will provide a full port list in the checklist.
- If fully air-gapped: we ship signed packages and image manifests you can push to your local registry.

3) Audit & logging
- Request-level audit logs can be delivered to S3-compatible buckets or pushed via HTTPS to your Splunk/Datadog collectors. Retention/formatting are configurable.

Attachment: network_diagram_v1.png (sample layout showing control plane, model hosts in private subnets, and optional on-prem ramp).

I’ll follow up with a one-page port/allowlist checklist by EOD 10/13 so Kevin’s team can pre-check firewall rules.

—Marissa
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
